children: Japan's November core consumer prices, which exclude fresh food, are expected to rise by around 2.7% from a year earlier, while the core-core measure, which strips out both fresh food and energy, is projected to increase around 2.3%, according to Okasan Securities estimates. Both indexes were up 2.2% in October, Friday's data showed. Price increases for items affected by Middle East tensions and artificial-intelligence demand stayed mild in the October report, though wholesale price data for the month shows supply-chain cost pressures are picking up again and will likely feed into retail prices going forward, the brokerage's economists say. (megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com)
